_README: docs/29 §5.2 — the signed-silence record. A key the glass detector cannot find in any
renderer is reported as a GLITCH until it appears here with a disposition AND a reason.
That is the whole mechanism: silence signed, never defaulted. Adding a line here is a
judgment you are putting your name to, not a way to quiet the tool.
Disposition is one of GLASS / EVIDENCE / REPORT / INTERNAL / DEAD (§5.2). Reason answers
docs/29 §5.3 step 4 — 'does this already have a home, anywhere, live or archival?' — and
names that home. DEAD means the producer should be deleted; a DEAD entry that outlives
the session that wrote it is itself a defect.

lanes.name: bench
lanes._note: The Repair Bench serves its own UI. This is the lane SYM-026 was found in: state() projected `runs` (18 omission runs on the S76 Beer) and bench.html referenced it zero times.

lanes.name: widget
lanes._note: Rust computes, JS renders. The `chunks_resumed` / `resumed` / `eta_s` heartbeat died on this wire (docs/29 §7.5).

lanes.name: converter
lanes._note: The converter writes the manifest and the receipts. Its readers are downstream CODE rather than a surface, so a hit here means 'something consumes it', which is weaker than 'a human sees it' — the bench and widget lanes then re-check whether the consumer projects it onward. `manifest.chunking.seams[]` (docs/29 §7.3) is the case this two-hop shape is built to catch.

bench:stream.reason: An outbound request parameter on the bench's ✦ assist call (bench.py:1134) — it tells Ollama not to stream. docs/29 §5.3 step 1: it exists only to feed another computation, so it is correctly silent and no human ever wants it on a surface. SCOPE NOTE, and it is the point of this entry: bench.py was NOT touched this session. This key entered the --since scope from `analyst.py`'s request body, which S79 edited for the residency fix, because the filter harvests key NAMES across the whole *.py diff and then attributes them to whichever lane has a producer using that name. That is the identical mis-scoping S79 diagnosed in the `bench:reason` entry below at 21:00 and then reproduced at its own close six hours later. docs/31 §5.2 item 7 — whether outbound request bodies are 'measured, stored values' at all — is UNSIGNED, and this is the second piece of evidence that they are not.

bench:keep_alive.reason: Outbound request parameter (bench.py:1134): the bench's assist deliberately sends keep_alive 0 so the model leaves VRAM after a single interactive call — correct there, unlike the analyst, whose calls are back-to-back (S79 residency fix). Control flow, never a surface. Same scope note as bench:stream: it arrived from analyst.py's diff, not from any change to the bench.

bench:prompt.reason: Outbound request parameter (bench.py:1135) — the text sent to the model. Its content is already visible to the operator: they typed it into the AI bar and the proposal comes back on the glass. Showing the assembled prompt would be chrome nobody asked for (docs/29 §5.3 step 5). Same scope note as bench:stream.

bench:reason.reason: The five-outcome triage's free-text reason (bench.py:667 triage, :678/:682 coverage). Its home is the opened zone/run card, not the chip row — docs/29 §5.3 step 3: a localizer is EVIDENCE, revealed when the card is open, never promoted to ambient chrome. NOTE ON SCOPE: this key surfaced under `--since 60acd77` only because dispositions.json's own `reason` fields entered the diff as added `"reason":` lines — a false positive of name-based scoping (the key was not added to a producer this session). Recorded as the honest disposition anyway rather than waved away, since the question it forces is the right one. The scoping weakness itself belongs on docs/31 §5.2's sheet.
